## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}

```

```{r load packages}
library(readxl)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
```
```{r import base data (LRAM 2019)}
excel_sheets("FoodAccessResearchAtlasData2019.xlsx")
lram2019 <- read_excel("FoodAccessResearchAtlasData2019.xlsx", sheet = "Food Access Research Atlas")
```
```{r check base data}
dim(lram2019)
head(lram2019)
names(lram2019)
class(lram2019$CensusTract)
```

```{r import 2019 population data (2019 ACS 5-year estimates)}
pop2019 <- read_csv("ACSDT5Y2019.B01003-Data.csv")
head(pop2019)
summary(pop2019)

pop2019 <- read_csv("ACSDT5Y2019.B01003-Data.csv") %>%
  slice(-1) %>%
  select(-starts_with("...")) %>%
  mutate(
    B01003_001E = as.numeric(B01003_001E),   # convert to actual numbers
    B01003_001M = as.numeric(B01003_001M)
  ) %>%
  rename(
    Population2019 = B01003_001E,
    MarginOfError_Pop = B01003_001M
  ) %>%
  mutate(CensusTract = str_remove(GEO_ID, "1400000US")) %>%
  select(CensusTract, Population2019)

head(pop2019)
str(pop2019)
summary(pop2019)
```

```{r import 2019 housing unit data (2019 ACS 5-year estimates)}
housing2019 <- read_csv("ACSDT5Y2019.B25001-Data.csv")
head(housing2019)
summary(housing2019)

housing2019 <- read_csv("ACSDT5Y2019.B25001-Data.csv") %>%
  slice(-1) %>%
  mutate(HousingUnits2019 = as.numeric(B25001_001E)) %>%
  mutate(CensusTract = str_remove(GEO_ID, "1400000US")) %>%
  select(CensusTract, HousingUnits2019)

head(housing2019)
str(housing2019)
```

```{r Merge Data (pop and housing - fine grained)}
merged_data <- lram2019 %>%
  left_join(pop2019, by = "CensusTract") %>%
  left_join(housing2019, by = "CensusTract")

head(merged_data)
sum(is.na(merged_data$Population2019))
sum(is.na(merged_data$HousingUnits2019))
```

```{r add wide scale data}
excel_sheets("2025-food-environment-atlas-data.xlsx")
stores <- read_excel("2025-food-environment-atlas-data.xlsx", sheet = "STORES", skip = 1)
restaurants <- read_excel("2025-food-environment-atlas-data.xlsx", sheet = "RESTAURANTS", skip=1)
stores_selected <- stores %>%
  select(FIPS, GROC20)

restaurants_selected <- restaurants %>%
  select(FIPS, FFR20)

food_combined <- stores_selected %>%
  left_join(restaurants_selected, by = "FIPS") %>%
  mutate(CountyFIPS = str_pad(as.character(FIPS), 5, pad = "0")) %>%
  select(-FIPS)

print(head(food_combined))
food_combined <- food_combined %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~na_if(., -9999)))
print(head(food_combined))
```

```{r merge all}
merged_data <- merged_data %>%
  mutate(CountyFIPS = substr(CensusTract, 1, 5)) %>%
  left_join(food_combined, by = "CountyFIPS")

dim(merged_data)
sum(is.na(merged_data$GROC20))
sum(is.na(merged_data$FFR20))
write_csv(merged_data, "merged_food_access_data_full.csv")

food_data_merged_2019 <- merged_data
food_data_merged_2019
```
